short: The English clergy agreed to surrender their legislative independence to King Henry VIII.
full:
On 15 May 1532, the Convocation of the English Church officially agreed to the Submission of the Clergy. Pressured heavily by King Henry VIII and an increasingly anti-clerical Parliament, church leaders relinquished their traditional right to assemble and enact canon law without express royal permission. Furthermore, they agreed to submit all existing church laws to a royal committee for review and potential veto.

This capitulation effectively broke the institutional and legislative independence of the Catholic Church in England. It paved the way for the total structural severance from Rome, culminating in the formal establishment of the Royal Supremacy two years later. The Submission demonstrated the Crown's unprecedented new ability to bend the spiritual estate to its political will, forever altering the English constitution.
